answer: Pay for marginal information, not for keys: a scoring pool pays each signed report exactly the drop in log-loss it causes. A Sybil fleet dumping identical forecasts into the shared report harbor adds nothing after the first copy, so every duplicate's payout sinks to its nadir of zero no matter how many identities it spins up; the surplus entries are a relic of the clone farm, worth nothing. The attacker still pays N access fees and compute while collecting zero marginal reward, so cloning loses money, while a genuinely novel signal keeps earning.
